📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Former Rangers and Sunderland head coach Michael Beale has broken his silence on his turbulent 177-day spell in charge of Belgian Pro League side Zulte Waregem after resigning last week.

Beale, 46, brought down the curtain on his short time at the Elindus Arena following the 4-1 defeat to Sint-Truidense last week, which made it six consecutive league defeats. Their worst run of results since October 7, 2018, they are just four points above the relegation zone.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

Sources indicate that his spell in Belgium was plagued by rumours of a breakdown in his relationship with senior figures at the club over Waregem’s direction and strategy. Beale actually started the campaign brightly, going unbeaten in their opening five games. However, their form swiftly deteriorated, and they have failed to register a victory since September 6.

His first managerial role since being sacked after just 12 games in charge at Sunderland almost three years ago, he exited Waregem with an identical record to the one he held at the Stadium of Light, with four wins, two draws, and six losses, meaning he left both sides with a 33.3% win rate after 12 games.

In a short statement confirming his departure, Waregem mentioned: “After several internal discussions between the head coach and the club, both parties decided to end their collaboration by mutual agreement.” Zulte Waregem are yet to appoint Beale’s permanent successor, with interim head coach Steve Colpaert expected to take charge of their league game vs Royal Antwerp at the weekend.

A week on from his departure, Beale penned an emotional farewell message to Waregem via his official Instagram page, writing: “Waregem, thankyou. It has been an honour and privilege to manage this club and I want to begin by thanking the fans for their incredible support. From day one, your passion and loyalty stood out and made coaching this club feel truly special. I will never forget the welcome you gave me and I have been overwhelmed by all your messages and kind words over the last few days.

It has been revealed that “This community has become a home to me and to everyone I met in the local shops, coffee houses, parks, restaurants and bars: thank you. Many of you have become true friends and you have made me feel completely one of your own. I also want to show my gratitude to the players and staff for their hard work, dedication and the special memories we created together. You have been a pleasure to work with and I wish you every success in the future.”.

Sources indicate that the ex-Rangers manager first joined Rangers as first-team coach during Steven Gerrard’s spell as manager at Ibrox. However, he left to join the former Liverpool icon in a similar role when he was appointed at Aston Villa in November 2021. Shortly afterwards, Beale took on his first managerial role with Queens Park Rangers.

In a recent development, he lasted just six months at Loftus Road before being poached by Rangers as a replacement for Giovanni van Bronckhorst. He struggled in the main role at Rangers, though, and was sacked in October 2023 before joining Sunderland three months later.

Gruda shone with a solo goal against the Serbs, as well as another goal and two assists against the Dutch.

His feat against Serbia impressed his manager. ‘It’s completely crazy. The defender in front of him? Poor guy!’ - the German manager exclaimed.

In this case, Liverpool have two allies who could push Brajan Gruda to join the English giants: Florian Wirtz and Jurgen Klopp.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Derek McInnes has stressed that Rangers have no intention of selling their key players in January as he looks to maintain the club’s growing momentum ahead of Saturday night’s Premiership clash with Motherwell.

The Ibrox boss believes retaining the core of his squad will be vital to Rangers’ silverware ambitions this season, insisting that the club has no desire to part with regular starters despite potential interest from elsewhere.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

While conceding that an offer too good to turn down would have to be considered, McInnes emphasised that Rangers are keen to avoid disruption to the squad when the winter transfer window opens.

Recent findings suggest that “We will be keeping them,” he declared emphatically. “We're not looking to move players out, certainly players who have been playing regularly. We want to shut that down really early. We know and understand that keeping that core of players and having that stability is so important for us.”.

Rangers return to league action against a Motherwell side McInnes claims is beginning to rediscover the qualities that made them such a formidable opponent last season under Jens Berthel Askou.

They head to Fir Park aiming to extend their 12-game unbeaten run, but McInnes anticipates a difficult test against a Motherwell side that has shown signs of improvement under Alfred Johansson’s care in recent weeks.

“I think they've started to look a wee bit more like that team that got a lot of success last year,” McInnes admitted. “They've got a lot of traits and similarities. They've lost two or three key players, but they still have the nucleus of that team and you can see they've got a clear idea of what they're trying to do.

“The difficulty when you go away from home is obvious. You've got to make sure you do so much right. It's not just about being good technically. You've got to make sure that all the other facets are there, that you need to compete right from the outset.”.

McInnes highlighted Rangers’ recent away win at St Mirren as a blueprint for Saturday’s encounter, adding: “Something similar will be required. If we want to get to where we want to get to this season, it's a game that presents us with three points. And we want to make sure we leave Motherwell with all three, if we can.”.

Rangers have kept eight clean sheets during their near two-month unbeaten run, with McInnes eager for his side to maintain their defensive solidity as they enter a demanding run of fixtures.

“I don't like it when we're too comfortable," he explained. “If we're four or five up and we’re deep into the second half, then I'll be all fine. But when the game is still in the balance, particularly away from home, and you're 1-0 up or 2-0 up, there's still work to do.

In a recent development, “We should be proud of that [clean sheets], but I thought we put it at risk a wee bit once or twice against St Mirren and I think it was unnecessary. We've got to make sure that we don't get complacent with what we're doing and we stay on top of the job.".

Industry observers note that with three consecutive home fixtures following Saturday's trip to North Lanarkshire, Rangers have an opportunity to build further momentum. McInnes, however, knows the immediate priority is on overcoming a rejuvenated Motherwell side.

“We're not expecting it to be straightforward,” he stated. “But I do expect us to bring a strong performance if we're going to win the game. I think everybody, certainly me and the staff, and I'm sure the supporters are the same, are starting to see a team that we think we can get behind and get a bit of confidence from.”.

There was positive news on the injury front following the international break, with Daisuke Yokota returning to training earlier this week alongside Ross McCrorie, while Lawrence Shankland and Cammy Devlin are continuing their rehabilitation through increased work on the grass.

This publication has requested interviews and so has the BBC’s Robin Grey – but nothing has transpired yet.

In a recent development, “And he's not doing it. In my opinion, he should front up because at the end of the day, he's the major boss. He's the owner.

Industry observers note that and Vessey, who has been captain and manager at Crawley, agreed. “It’s been four weeks of silence, pretty much. Just be honest. People just want you to be honest with them.

In a recent development, say something like ‘we're trying to recruit because of the position we're in, we're finding it a bit difficult’. ‘We're relying on Kevin Blackwell to hopefully improve that position so that we can get a permanent appointment’. Hearts’ versatile attacker Rogers Mato says the Tynecastle dressing room is determined to end the club’s 14-year wait for a major trophy after seeing the title slip through their fingers in the final minutes of last season.

Mato, 23, played just three league games for Hearts after arriving on an initial loan from North Macedonian outfit FK Vardar last January, but has featured regularly for the Gorgie side this season after making his move permanent in the summer by penning a three-year contract in July.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

Originally signed as a wide forward, the Ugandan international was deployed as a left-back against Turkish outfit Trabzonspor in the Europa League earlier this month, with Hearts’ injury crisis seeing Mato pitted against former Liverpool icon, Mo Salah. However, he admits it’s another ex-Anfield hero, Senegal international Sadio Mane, that he takes inspiration from as he looks ahead to the African Cup of Nations in his homeland next summer.

“I grew up just watching the other players on TV and sneaking in the stadiums,” Mato told RG. “I didn't even have a chance to be like a ball boy to give them the balls in the national team. I only did that on the club level. But wearing the national team jersey is a big responsibility, we're representing our families, our dream, and millions of Ugandans.

“Mane is my all-time favourite African player. I would love to wear the captain's armband. I would love to lead my country. We grow by responsibilities, not by age. So, that would have a massive impact and would be a massive confidence booster for me to be leading the nation to glory.”.

The 23-year-old claims he is using the pain of defeat to fuel another of his major dreams - bringing silverware at Tynecastle. Refusing to concede his side are out of the title race this season despite being 11 points behind league leaders Celtic, he admits the crushing way that a first top flight title win since 1960 trophy was ripped from their grasp by two late Hoops goal on the final day last season still stings.

In a recent development, “It's been ups and downs [since joining Hearts],” he admits. “Coming from Macedonia, playing 90-plus minutes and then coming on for Hearts and playing for 13 minutes in three games and 13 minutes in the second half of the season. It's been ups and downs, but with patience, everything will come to an end.

It has been revealed that “I just had to come here and wait for my time, but every time we just have to be patient. I needed to work hard on myself, work hard for the team, so I can get more game time. It's all about mentality. You have to adapt to any coach that comes your way. If you don't adapt, you're dead as a footballer. Last season was hectic and brutal for the team, for the fans. Those last minutes [vs Celtic], it was a heartbreak for everyone, for every Hearts fan. It was a total disaster.

Sources indicate that “But we're looking forward to give it all this season. But suddenly we got a lot of injuries here and there, but those who are still fit, we're trying our best to still keep [the title race] alive for our friends, our brothers who are injured, so they can come and join us [when they're back]. Because we can't let it down, we still have to keep the hopes for the first place.".

#49073. Industry News: Thomas Tuchel is now embracing traditional English values - clarity has helped England understand who they are, and now they can beat the best, writes CRAIG HOPE

📅 16 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (941 w)

Industry News: Thomas Tuchel is now embracing traditional English values - clarity has helped England understand who they are, and now they can beat the best, writes CRAIG HOPE

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (941 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 16:57 EST, 16 November 2026 | Updated: 16:57 EST, 16 November 2026.
  • Industry observers note that thomas Tuchel has always liked what he sees from his England players on the training pitch.
  • It is why, when the squad reconvened at St George’s Park in September, Tuchel used the meeting room as much as he did the grass to address that disparity in delivery.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By CRAIG HOPE, CHIEF FOOTBALL REPORTER.

Published: 16:57 EST, 16 November 2026 | Updated: 16:57 EST, 16 November 2026.

Industry observers note that thomas Tuchel has always liked what he sees from his England players on the training pitch. Less so, at times, inside a stadium. It is a contradiction with which he has wrestled since the World Cup, when performances on the whole left him underwhelmed, save for the collective spirit and individual excellence that rescued results.

It is why, when the squad reconvened at St George’s Park in September, Tuchel used the meeting room as much as he did the grass to address that disparity in delivery.

It has been revealed that at the same time, the elephant in the corner of the auditorium was the German’s own comments about the DNA of English players compared to the likes of Spain, and fundamentally them lacking the coding to protect possession and, therefore, valuable leads. He asked Harry Kane, Jude Bellingham and others for their thoughts.

The message back from his players was this – let us be better at being us, not them. Interestingly, that was Tuchel’s mantra upon his appointment, one of embracing traditional English values. Amid the World Cup fallout, though, he had wandered in a daze down a rabbit hole of genetics, focusing on what his team cannot do as opposed to what they can.

It has been revealed that tuchel, his staff and his players are tacticians and technicians, not scientists. If the intricacies of DNA do not allow them to be Spain, then don’t be. Be England, they determined. That is not to say kick and rush, bark and bite. After all, Kane is officially the best player in the world right now and Bellingham, unofficially, is playing as well as anyone on the planet.

In a recent development, rather, there needed to be clarity – this is what we are and this is how we beat the best. On Sunday night in Madrid, England beat the very best. It was a victory born from those hours on the training field and in conference, and even more spent by Tuchel and his assistant Anthony Barry during their post-tournament review in a St George’s Park war room. They knew then that this was not a case of rip it up and start again, more so mend the tears and give the likes of Bellingham a blank sheet to impact where, and how, he sees best.

Thomas Tuchel is embracing England's DNA and reaping the rewards following the World Cup.

England can now beat the best, which they showed against Spain in a fantastic victory.

Industry observers note that there was no radical strategical change, but there was a new doctrine, principles that should underpin whatever the in-game circumstance – off-the-ball running, a high press, filling in for a team-mate who has seized a moment to improvise elsewhere, such as the full backs. Ben White scoring England’s third on Sunday and Lewis Hall completing four more dribbles than Lamine Yamal were examples of Tuchel’s allowance for greater intuition. Be you, not Spain.

It has been revealed that kane, informally at least, has also been promoted beyond captain, a bridge between management and dressing-room. To see him in a semi-coaching and cajoling capacity on the touchline after he was taken off in the 78th minute against Spain was to witness this elevation.

Recent findings suggest that but even if England had conceded a late equaliser at the Metropolitano Stadium, it would not have mattered. Not when it comes to measuring post World Cup improvement. To have drawn comparison with Argentina and that second-half collapse would have been unfair and inaccurate. The semi-final was 11 versus 11 and so let us judge this game on the same terms. And what did England do with a 1-0 lead and 11 players? They attacked. And attacked again. For all of the tweaks Tuchel and Barry have made to the structure of training and the team’s set-up, this was evidence of them learning from a mistake, as much as the head coach will be loath to admit.

Ezri Konsa, however, did reveal there was a definite instruction to keep attacking Spain when Tuchel addressed the team at half-time.

‘The instruction was to keep going at them,’ noted the defender. ‘Don’t stop. To keep our foot on the pedal. That is what we did. Argentina was different, different circumstances. But it was not just half-time. We went 1-0 up and Harry, our captain, told us to keep going and to keep our foot on the pedal too.'.

Before Jarell Quansah’s needless mistake and Elliot Anderson’s subsequent dismissal in the 63rd minute, the game was not in the balance in any way. As a live observer of almost every Tuchel match since his arrival, this was the best performance of his reign. In fact, it’s not even close.

And yet, so much still comes back to Bellingham. England would not have won without him. He terrified Spain, perhaps given their intimate knowledge of his powers. Beating the best is as much a mental challenge as it is physical, and Bellingham believed. He made England believe, too. His swagger. His majesty. And yes, his skill. He won the corner for Konsa’s headed second and created the third for White. He then dropped into midfield when down to ten and battled and organised like a captain.

Sources indicate that bellingham has bought into the collective under Tuchel and, with that, his team-mates are buying into his big ideas. For now, they don’t come much bigger than what England achieved in Madrid.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Carter White | 19 Nov 2026 12:49, Last updated: 19 Nov 2026 16:37.

Life without Vitor Matos begins for Swansea City on Saturday afternoon, when fellow promotion hopefuls West Bromwich Albion visit Swansea.com Stadium for a Championship battle.

The Swans have lost their Portuguese mastermind to Ligue 1 following a poor run of form prior to the international break, whereas the Baggies come into this South Wales clash full of confidence.

After being linked to vacant roles at Crystal Palace and Sporting Lisbon over the past month, Swansea head coach Matos has been poached by Ligue 1 outfit Strasbourg, leaving the Welsh side without a permanent manager this weekend.

The 38-year-old's departure comes after an overall impressive start to the season for the Swans, however, they have lost four of their past five second-tier matches, falling to defeat by Birmingham City on November 7.

Collecting just three points from Matos's final five games at the helm, Swansea have slid down to sixth place in the Championship standings after 15 matches, still just three points behind the league leaders.

Alarmingly, a once-watertight defence has conceded 11 goals across its last five contests in the second tier, although the Swans were excellent in their most recent home match, smashing Blackburn Rovers by a 4-0 scoreline.

Former Swansea defender Ashley Williams is expected to join Leon Britton and Kris O'Leary in an interim coaching group on Saturday afternoon, when the hosts will look to extend their unbeaten home run against West Brom to eight matches.

Concerns regarding a potential relegation to League One in the spring feel a million miles away from The Hawthorns right now, with West Brom targeting an unlikely promotion push at the top of the Championship.

Since losing to pacesetters Birmingham on October 10, the Baggies have strung together an impressive six-match unbeaten run (W4 D2) in the second tier, enjoying a standout home success last time out.

James Morrison's troops took full advantage of a wounded Lions pack in the Black Country on November 7, when Isaac Price, Jayson Molumby and Norway international Felix Horn Myhre all netted in the demolition of Millwall.

Yet to be defeated by a club below them in the league standings so far this season, West Brom are currently occupying fifth position, just a single point behind Blues, Middlesbrough and Stoke City at the summit of the division.

The Albion were simply awful on the road during the opening months of 2026 but have improved massively under the stewardship of Morrison, who has masterminded wins at Wrexham (2-1) and West Ham United (3-1) over the past few weeks.

Swansea City Championship form:.

West Bromwich Albion Championship form:.

Swansea were unsuccessful in their appeal of Marko Stamenic's red card at Birmingham prior to the international pause.

As a result, the Latest Zealander is sidelined for the next three matches, including the South Wales derby against Cardiff City on November 29.

Goncalo Franco and Stephen Welsh are both doubts for this weekend's game due to muscular problems.

West Brom suffered a major fitness blow during the two-week break, with influential midfielder Ousmane Diakite picking up a calf injury whilst on duty for Mali.

The much-improved 26-year-old faces at least eight weeks on the sidelines, joining fellow midfielder Toby Collyer in the medical room.

The Baggies are also short on options in defence, with Noah Galves (knee) out of action, but captain George Campbell is available for selection.

Swansea City possible starting lineup:.

Vigouroux; Lissah, Cabango, Seelt, Tymon; Widell, Fulton, Iorpenda; Yeo, Eom, Idah.

West Bromwich Albion possible starting lineup:.

O'Leary; Pereira, Mepham, Phillips, Styles; Whitwell, Molumby, Nzingoula, Price; Heggebo, Morgan.

Rocked by the sudden departure of Matos, Swansea will be chasing home comforts in South Wales this weekend.

Even without Diakite, West Brom should be good enough for a share of the spoils with the managerless Swans.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Danny Hollands’ side went out after a 3-2 reverse to the SCFL outfit, meaning the Rocks are now out of all the cup competitions.

It has been revealed that the loss came on the back of a 2-1 derby day victory over Littlehampton Town in the Isthmian South Central division on Saturday. And the Nye Camp aces get the chance to improve their points tally on Saturday when they host Hayes & Yeading.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

The victory – after two reverses on the spin -- against the lowly Sportsfield outfit maintained the club’s spot in third in the league standings, with Egham Town top and Jersey Bulls, who the Rocks visit next week, second.

Another positive to come out of that game was the full return of striker Cal Laycock after a long lay-off -- and similarly against United a bonus was the goal-scoring return of long-term absentee Billy Allcock.

It was assistant manager Ben Kneller who spoke to the club’s YouTube channel about the cup exit to Eastbourne, against whom youngsters such as Dennis Wooldridge, Noah Light, Toby Kingswell, Archie Bennett and Louie Williams all featured -- and some of those had actually played the night before in an U18s game, too.

According to recent reports, kneller stated: “We need to keep moving forward but all in all, if we were stood here having the conversation last year when we first game (to manage) and we said, 'listen, we are going to be third or fourth in the league come mid-November, we have lost two games in 26, but you're out of the cups, would you have taken it? You probably would have done. We need to step back to see where we are, (compared) to where we were.

It has been revealed that "It was a little bit of real reality check after Saturday when we had 1,300 in (and beat our local rivals). We are not happy to be out and not happy with a few in the dressing room – but there are positives within the negatives.

According to recent reports, "Noah is a very intelligent footballer (for instance). They (some u18s) train with us on a Thursday and they are around the environment all the time and just because they don't feature in games they are still in around along with others.

Recent findings suggest that “We want to progress young players in the area and that is what Bognor is all about. It's not all about winning this and winning that, it is very much about building from the base and we believe in that. From our side of things there is a pathway for the 18s and we have shown it.".

On being out of all the cups, he added: "We would like to have a cup run but you can never guarantee it but we would have liked to deliver it Maybe we strip the squad back a little more now we are out of the cups and we realign.".

Here’s Liam Goodley’s full report from the Senior Cup defeat.

Bognor were knocked out of the Sussex Senior Cup under the lights at Nyewood Lane as their makeshift side were put to the test by well organised, Eastbourne United.

According to recent reports, tommy Block went into the book early on for his challenge after a back pass. Rhyle Overden crossed it in from the free-kick but straight into the arms of Archie Bennett in the Bognor goal.

Charlie Gunson latched on to a loose ball after a long ball into the area and his strike was deflected away from the back legs of a defender on 11 minutes. Archie Bennett did well to stop two players twice after James Hull's cross that was hit low into the box on 15 minutes, keeping the scoreline goalless.

Gunson did well to wind into the box but his shot was deflected into the path of Ollie Lovell who was also denied by an Eastbourne body. Joe Overy did well on the attack for the visitors. He cut inside after some swift passing play but fired it over the crossbar from outside the area.

Anderson hooked the ball high into the area from the freekick. Block was unmarked as he leapt up to head that towards goal. The ball looped up kindly for the goalkeeper though.

In a recent development, sorge Nones did all the hard work winding his way through the area but blasted over the bar with his left foot on 37 minutes. Secka had to punch away a dipping direct freekick frm Gunson off the left side on 41 minutes. HT 0-0.

Recent findings suggest that changes at half-time saw Block, Benny Read and Gunson come off for Josh Batt, Toby Kingswell and Ethan Robb. Batt got the ball forward to Louie Williams, but after rounding his marker he fired it low and into the grateful arms of Secka from a tight angle on 54 minutes.

Bognor made another change on 60 minutes that saw Maadhav Jagota replaced by Callum Laycock and Lovell came off for Billy Allcock.

Recent findings suggest that A swift move down the left saw Eastbourne United take the lead on 67 minutes. Overy used his pace to run down the left before diverting a low ball into the area and ex-Rock Callum Barlow knocked it in from close range.

Williams set Kingswell on his way down the right wing but Kingswell smacked his cross out of play for a goal kick in a poor half for Bognor.

Industry observers note that robb's free-kick curled dangerously into the area on 78 minutes. The ball was knocked down wide of the right post as the goalkeeper watched it roll past the right post.

James Stone, off the bench, did really well to compose himself running in front of defence before powerfully driving the ball into the net beyond a diving Bennett on 79 minutes, extending United's lead.

Harvey Whyte put in a great delivery from the right and Laycock got their ahead of his marker to get something onto it, and managed to divert the ball low, of which Secka managed to save low to his right.

Another forward ball saw Billy Allcock run through and his first strike was blocked before he followed up to net it on the rebound on 84 minutes for 2-1.

However, that reduced lead didn't last long as Stone worked hard on the right before putting it on a plate for Overy to knock into the net on 85 minutes.

In a recent development, bognor got another goal back direct from Robb's corner as Laycock netted it with his head on 91 minutes. Bognor were attacking towards the end for a last gasp equaliser but Eastbourne United were good defensively to stave off the danger late on.

So the Rocks were knocked out of the Sussex Senior Cup at the third round stage and are now able to fully focus on their league campaign with some massive games coming up, including next up, a home tie against Hayes & Yeading United this Saturday (21st November, 3pm).

According to recent reports, rocks: Bennett, Read, Wooldridge, Anderson, Whyte, Block, Jagota, Lovell, Williams, Gunson, Light. Subs (all used): Batt, Laycock, Allcock, Robb, Kingswell.

Industry observers note that "Tommy Gravesen would play Call of Duty when I was at Celtic,” mentioned McGeady. “We had a group, so we'd go home from training and play it. Tommy would never give us his gamertag. I don't know why, but I don't think he wanted us playing with him. But apparently he was like third or fourth in the world at Call of Duty on team deathmatch.

"Somebody managed to get his gamertag and added him and he had 45 days of playing time. 45 days of playing time! Sources indicate that however, despite the popularity of GTA VI, the 40-year-old doesn’t expect any current professionals to follow in the footsteps Celtic, Everton and Real Madrid. McGeady admits he has seen several players take portable games consoles on the team coach when headed to away games, and the ex-Celtic and Hibs man has warned the younger generation to not follow Gravesen’s example.

“I don't think GTA VI would be a problem because anybody that brings a portable PlayStation or a portable Xbox, they're obsessed with it anyway, aren't they?” McGeady mentioned, speaking to BOYLE Sports. I've been on buses before and it's like lads will get the PlayStations out and it's like FIFA or Call of Duty or it's Fortnite, whatever it is. Lads do that anyway, they're obsessed with it anyway.

"So I don't think GTA VI is going to create a new breed of a new market of players who are just going to start playing PlayStation. I think the people that already play it will play it anyway. I think most footballers are fairly responsible and most Premier League footballers are fairly responsible. I don't think it's going to take over their life. Maybe for the younger players it could be an concern because they can be addicted to these games.”.

“They should have been a goal in front from a mistake by us, then within 30 seconds we were 1-0 up.

“The wet/sticky surface made it difficult for both sides who looked to play but overall I think the neutrals got their money’s worth.

“It was nice to make five changes from Saturday, get minutes into lads returning from injury and reach the quarter-finals.

It completed a perfect week for the Bears after Saturday’s 2-0 Isthmian South East win at Margate, in which Luke Bejashvili scored both. Heath host Hastings on Saturday.

Here is Andrew Crisp’s Heath v Heath match report….

On paper this midweek trip to Southern Combination League leaders Haywards Heath Town looked a potential banana skin for Chris Simmons’ Broadbridge Heath.

The hosts may be a division below the Bears but they have made a great start to the season, five points clear at the top of the Premier Division, unbeaten at home after ten matches and having knocked cup favourites Brighton & Hove Albion out by 2-0 in an earlier round, but things don’t always work out as some may predict.

Simmons made five changes to the starting line-up that won 2-0 at Margate three days earlier, four at the back including Bailey Cotton on his way back from injury and making his first start since September and Ollie Rawlins making just his second start of the season after injury.

Broadbridge Heath got off to a great start on 3 minutes when Ben Holden received the ball on the halfway line and drove forward into the Haywards Heath half before playing the ball out wide to Ben Royall advancing down the left, and the Bears full-back cut inside and struck a low right foot shot from distance into the bottom right corner of the net.

The Bears doubled their lead on 24 minutes with Holden and Royal involved again: this time Holden, in the centre of the park, played the ball into the feet of Royall with his back to goal and closely marked, the Bears defender turned his marker and ran towards the Haywards Heath penalty area before striking a low left foot shot across the goal into the far corner.

At the other end Jack Barnes powered a header from a corner onto the top of the crossbar and Bears skipper Brad Peters reacted quickly to clear the ball off the goal-line but it was Broadbridge Heath who increased their lead on 32 minutes.

An interchange of passes ended with Luke Bejashvili playing the ball into the feet of Holden who played a first time pass to Ollie Rawlins some 25 yards out and with his back to goal and the Heath striker turned sharply to power a right foot shot into the bottom right corner giving the hosts’ keeper Charlie Roberts no chance of stopping.

Minutes later Broadbridge Heath’s Sal Marino played a defence-splitting ball to send Charlie Connell through on goal but Roberts was off his line promptly to force the player wide of goal and instead Connell played the ball back into the path of Rawlins on the edge of the “D” who blasted his shot high and wide.

A minute before the break the hosts pulled a goal back when Josh Wright crossed the ball from the right flank into the Broadbridge Heath penalty area where the ball bobbled around the six yard box before falling kindly to Charlie Meehan to tap in from close range.

Broadbridge Heath restored their three goal advantage almost immediately when a long ball was played down the left channel and chased down by Rawlins who delivered a left foot cross into the path of Zac Young, who hit a sweet left foot shot from 12 yards which was saved brilliantly by Roberts. Young pounced on the loose ball and was brought down by a clumsy challenge, and the match referee immediately pointed to the penalty spot with nobody from Haywards Heath questioning the decision and Young got up to convert the spot kick for his sixth goal of the season to make it 1-4 at the break.

According to recent reports, haywards Heath needed an early second half goal to get back into the game but the reverse happened 2 minutes into the restart when Broadbridge Heath goalkeeper Stan Williamson intercepted a right wing cross and threw the ball out quickly to Young in the centre of the park. He drove forward to the halfway line before playing the ball wide right to Charlie Connell, who took the ball towards the goal-line and then delivered a right wing pass across the goal to Rawlins to score from six yards.

Heath added a sixth goal on the hour mark when Rawlins received the ball wide on the right and played a long ball towards the far post where it was headed in by Connell from 8 yards to near enough secure the win for the Bears.

Simmons was able to swap his players around which included the welcome return to the side for Mason Doughty, the Heath striker with eight goals from 13 games this season has missed the last eight games through injury.

Haywards Heath added a second in time added-on when a combination of Wright and Barnes won the ball off a Bears defender and linked up well down the right channel before the ball was played inside to Barnes who finished with aplomb.

BBH: Williamson, Cotton (Thiselton 60), Royall, Marino, Peters, Salaam (Richardson 65), Bejashvili, Holden, Rawlins (Doughty 70), Connell (Hards 61), Young.

Aberdeen chief executive Adrian Bevington is confident the club are set for a period of stability following the appointment of Mario Frick as manager on a two-and-a-half-year contract.

It has been revealed that the Pittodrie club have had three managers this year alone. Four of the last five appointments failed to reach the 50-match mark. Stephen Robinson, Frick’s predecessor, lasted just 28 games.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

“That (stability) is the objective here," noted Bevington, who himself only joined Aberdeen less than three months ago. "What I would say is we have gone through a really robust process. It wasn't just looking at one or two names. The wider search to begin with was extensive then we narrowed it down.”.

The former Club England managing director admitted the process of identifying a new manager began before Robinson was relieved of his duties after the recent 4-0 home defeat to Hibs.

Industry observers note that “Any club nowadays, or most clubs, would always have some prep work going on, just as a matter of course,” he stated. I think it's very difficult for clubs to be able to react to a situation if they've not already had some prep work going on. That's not any criticism of any individual manager.”.

Industry observers note that bevington stressed that Frick had not been appointed on the advice of players. Goalkeeper Marius Muller has been reported as claiming he first suggested the former Luzern manager’s name to sporting director Lutz Pfannenstiel. “We had some player conversations,” noted Bevington. “But they weren’t the decision makers.”.

Sources indicate that stuart Duff, the Youth Phase manager, has been promoted to Frick’s first-team coaching staff, while Craig Hinchcliffe remains goalkeeper coach. Bevington stressed it was vital for Frick to be supported by those with knowledge of the club’s youth players.

In a recent development, aberdeen at the moment has 24 players out on loan with various clubs, including striker Alfie Bavidge and full-back Dylan Lobban at Inverness Caledonian Thistle and Dunfermline respectively. There has been a clamour for Bavidge and Lobban to return.

It has been revealed that “There's conversations going on at the moment as to what we're going to do moving forward,” stated Bevington. I believe that we have capability to recall certainly a number of the players. I'd need to look at every individual contract.”.

By Matt Law | 19 Nov 2026 13:21.

The latest instalment of the Seville derby will take place at Estadio Ramon on Saturday evening, as Sevilla and Real Betis lock horns in La Liga.

Sevilla have historically dominated this fixture, but Real Betis have had the better of the recent meetings between the two, losing just one of their last eight contests with the White and Reds.

Sevilla have a record of five wins, three draws and four defeats from their 12 league matches this season, with 18 points leaving them in sixth position in the La Liga table.

Luis Garcia Plaza's side have only picked up one point from their last two league games, though, losing at Getafe at the start of November before drawing 0-0 with Alaves in their last fixture in front of their own fans before the international break.

Los Nervionenses have not managed to finish fourth in Spain's top flight since 2021-22, and there is no getting away from the fact that it has been a difficult few seasons for the club, finishing 12th, 14th, 17th and 13th in their last four campaigns.

However, Sevilla are currently showing form that could see them claim a European finish, which would be a major step forward given their recent troubles.

The White and Reds have won 61, lost 39 and drawn 35 of their previous 135 matches against Real Betis in all competitions, with their last success over their Seville rivals coming at home in October 2024.

Real Betis have claimed seven points from the last three league matches against Sevilla, including a 2-0 victory at Estadio Ramon last season, while they have lost just once to their rivals since February 2022.

Manuel Pellegrini's side recorded a 2-0 win over Elche in their last league match on November 8, before beating Navalcarnero 3-2 in the Copa del Rey four days later.

El Glorioso have won eight, drawn two and lost two of their 12 league matches this season to collect 26 points, which has left them in fourth spot in the division, eight points ahead of Sevilla leading into this weekend's Seville derby.

It has been a busy opening few months of the season for Real Betis given that Pellegrini's team are also playing in the Champions League; a strong start to their league stage has left them 11th in the table, claiming nine points from four matches.

The Seville team finished fifth in Spain's top flight last season and will again be expecting to challenge for a spot high up the division this term.

Real Betis form (all competitions):.

Sevilla will welcome Manu Bueno back into their squad on Saturday following a suspension, but Marcao, Peque and Miguel Sierra are again likely to miss out through injury.

Ruben Vargas is also a doubt due to the issue that forced him off against Alaves, which could mean that Chidera Ejuke is introduced into the starting side.

Robbie Ure is pushing to be introduced at centre-forward, but a tough start to his career with Sevilla has seen him manage just one goal in 12 league appearances.

Real Betis, meanwhile, remain without the services of Facundo Bernal through suspension.

Diego Llorente and Cucho Hernandez are also major doubts for the visitors on Saturday.

Troy Parrott is expected to continue through the middle for the away side, while Isco and Antony are also likely to retain their positions in the first XI.

Sevilla possible starting lineup:.

Vlachodimos; Iglesias, Sangante, Salas, Suazo; Fofana, Agoume; Ejuke, Romero, Correia; Stassin.

Real Betis possible starting lineup:.

Valles; Bellerin, Bartra, Natan, Garcia; Fornals, Roca; Antony, Isco, Ezzalzouli; Parrott.

This is a tough match to call, especially off the back of an international break. Cases can be made for either side to win it, but we believe that a tight match will finish all square.

  • Published: 17:35 EST, 16 November 2026 | Updated: 17:41 EST, 16 November 2026.
  • Andy Robertson admitted Scotland don’t have time to get things right under Sebastien Pocognoli after the team were humbled by Switzerland on the night of the skipper’s record 103rd cap.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By JOHN MCGARRY, SCOTTISH CHIEF SPORTS FEATURE WRITER.

Published: 17:35 EST, 16 November 2026 | Updated: 17:41 EST, 16 November 2026.

Andy Robertson admitted Scotland don’t have time to get things right under Sebastien Pocognoli after the team were humbled by Switzerland on the night of the skipper’s record 103rd cap.

John McGinn warned this week it could take the Scots up to 18 months to fully grasp the Belgian’s tactical plans.

But serious questions are now being asked of Pocognoli after his team were swept aside in a miserable 4-0 defeat to a much-changed Swiss side.

The result, combined with Slovenia’s 3-0 win over North Macedonia, ended Scotland’s already scant hopes of a Nations League promotion play-off spot and condemned them to pot three in next month’s Euro 2028 draw.

Robertson was hoping for a night to remember as he overtook Kenny Dalglish as the country’s most capped player but was clearly furious as the Scots crumbled in St Gallen.

Asked if it was going to take time for things to click under Pocognoli, he told the BBC: ‘I don’t think you’ve got time in international football, you have to do it.

Scotland skipper Andy Robertson laments a night to forget on the occasion of his 103rd cap.

‘These supporters who travel everywhere, are they going to give us time? No. Are the people inside Hampden going to give us time? No. Are the people outside Hampden, who are going to be critical and rightly so? No.

‘We don’t have time, the players do not have time, we have got to step up.

‘We have a long break now to March, which is not a good thing, and it is going to be a tough one to swallow.

‘We really need to step up again. In international football, you do not have time.’.

After an unconvincing start to his reign, Pocognoli needed a statement victory to convince sceptical fans that he is the right man for the job.

Despite a promising start, the rot set in after Lewis Ferguson’s 22nd minute own-goal.

The Swiss, missing a host of key players, went further ahead with goals from Winsley Boteli, Alvyn Sanches and Zeki Amdouni.

Almost 12 months on from the famous night when Steve Clarke’s side beat Denmark to reach the World Cup, the Tartan Army will be looking towards the European qualifiers with trepidation.

Robertson is tackled by Switzerland's Zachary Athekame on a night of few positives.

Robertson said: ‘First half, I thought we were in the game. We lost a stupid goal but I thought we had chances and it could have been 2-1 at half-time.

‘By the time you get to 50 minutes and you are 3-0 down, that can’t happen in international football.

‘We were playing a good team but I felt we were in the game, it is a really tough night for us.’.

Pocognoli also felt the final scoreline was harsh and rued his side’s inability to make the most of the opportunities they created.

‘The score is heavy with the 4-0, but I don’t think it’s a reflection of the game, if I’m really honest and objective,’ noted Pocognoli.

‘I think we had some very good moments, we started like we wanted, aggressive away from home. I think we played a good first half, we created chances, we were dominant in some moments and we faced Switzerland with different shapes and adapted well from the first minute.

Sebastien Pocognoli will now face some searching questions over his suitability for the job.

Sources indicate that ‘I think we conceded the goal from maybe one of the first chances they had. We also created chances but we were not clinical in that moment in the box.

It has been revealed that ‘In the second half, yeah, we started poorly from the first minute, a poor corner we gave away. Then you feel that, OK, we will get punished.

‘But I think when we made the substitutions, they made an impact, and we should have scored two goals in that period.

‘At the end, it’s a bad feeling, the score, but I think that the players try to do their best and create moments that we want to see.’.

For Eastbourne United it has to be between THAT FA Vase semi-final, beating Crawley Town in the Sussex Senior Cup, or, on the other side of that coin, the following Senior Cup game, where Bognor put seven past Simon Rowland’s men.

Spool forward 12 years, and United had a chance at restoring their good name in West Sussex, again in the Senior Cup.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

After a deluge on the way to the game, the United faithful were pleasantly surprised to see a pleasant evening for this step 4 v step 5 encounter.

As the referee got the match underway, it became immediately obvious that Anthony Storey’s boys were giving no quarter at all to the higher league team – Joe Overy running head down at the defence time and again as Charlie Ball, Callum Barlow and James Hull all went close top opening the scoring, with no real penetration from Bognor until the 20th minute, when Zach Robitaille and Dan Hull combined to clear off the line.

On the half hour, Overy decided to go it alone, his shot going just over the bar. Jorge Nones was looking very lively indeed and was unfortunate not to score, the Bognor keeper again earning his corn with a point blank save.

As the teams went in 0-0 at half time, nerves were showing among the Bognor crowd – maybe the lower league team will run out of steam?

Had they done their homework, they would know that Eastbourne United are one of the fittest teams in the SCFL Premier, and so it was that as the teams came out for the second half, if anything United had stepped their game up.

Industry observers note that james Hull had picked up a nasty cut in the first half and was replaced by the lively Freddie Jones on the hour. Almost straight away, Overy crossed for Barlow who made no mistake against his old club, to the absolute horror of the home support.

Bognor made a triple change in response, but to be honest did not really look to have an answer. James Stone replaced Barlow a few minutes later, and within minutes Ball broke down the right, his cross finding Stone for a great finish and 2-0. The upset was definitely on the cards.

According to recent reports, alieu Secka saved well from Cal Laycock, but with 5 minutes to go, the lifeline appeared and it was 2-1. United were not rattled – quite the opposite as Jones went straight up the other end and crossed for Overy to make it 3-1.

Alfie Gander replaced Ball as the game moved to 6 minutes of added time. Right at the end Bognor snuck a second goal, but it was too late, it made for an exciting last couple of minutes, but everyone knew that the game was up, indeed as the referee blew the final whistle there was generous applause from the Rocks supporters after a game played in a very good atmosphere.

Eastbourne United are in the quarter-finals and ready for another adventure in the next round.

On Saturday Guernsey are the visitors to the Oval for a 2pm kick-off, another match that will be vital in United’s promotion push.

Sources indicate that eastbourne Town’s Senior Cup interest is over. Sonny Walsh’s goal wasn’t enough to prevent a 2-1 defeat to Lewes at The Saffrons, also on Tuesday night.

In a recent development, but there was better news for Jude Macdonald’s team in the Isthmian South East last Saturday – they drew 1-1 at Sheppey, with Alfie Rogers their scorer. That ended a run of eight league defeats on the trot for Town and took them off bottom spot, now occupied by Horley.

Macdonald’s men host Whitstable tomorrow.

Industry observers note that right, where were we? Three weeks on from the fifth round of Premier League fixtures in which the champions Arsenal were beaten 3-0 by Brighton and todays’ visitors, Leeds United, who remain unbeaten, drew in a tepid goalless fixture with Crystal Palace, we finally get to the sixth. As worrying as the result was at the Amex, Arsenal still created a shedload of chances and last season they were the one club that battered Leeds in both games – first early in the season when they were playing four at the back and before Dominic Calvert-Lewin, a late signing, was fully fit, and then later after they had successfully switched to a “base formation” of three centre-backs and the tactical flexibility that allowed.

It was a 5-0 tanking in August and 4-0 in January, so to say Leeds travel to a ground at which they have never won more in hope than expectation would be as true as much as it is hackneyed. Adding to a sense of foreboding and thanks to Opta’s excellent Jonny Cooper, we also have to take into account the fact that Leeds, floodlight kings, have not won a Premier League match kicking off before 3pm since August 2022 and have not won a match in London since beating Brentford in May that year to save themselves from relegation. However, they do boast the division’s best defensive record – three goals conceded – and the No1 ranked goalkeeper in James Trafford who has a save percentage of 87. For all the sense of doom, though, Leeds have become a very good side and their spine – Trafford–Muharemovic–Ampadu–Calvert-Lewin marries steel and class.

Arsenall need no fanfare. Until the set-back in dear old Sussex by the sea, they had looked formidable most of the time and will have been champing at the bit to get back out there and prove it was an aberration. Mikel Arteta mentioned he has doubts about Declan Rice, Kai Havertz and Ezri Konsa but Ben White, Max Dowman and Chrsthian Mosquera are all available. For Leeds Joe Rodon is still out and Dan James was injured on international duty but Harry Wilson and Jean-Matteo Bahoya returned to training after knocks this week and Daniel Farke was relatively optimistic about their prospects.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Lewis Nolan | 19 Nov 2026 13:23.

The next instalment of the Borussen derby takes place at Borussia Park when Borussia Dortmund travel to face Borussia Monchengladbach in the Bundesliga on Saturday.

Dortmund come into the clash in second place with 21 points, trailing league-leaders Bayern Munich due to goal difference, whereas the hosts are last in 18th place with just four points.

Gladbach's situation is precarious but not irrecoverable, with the club's tally of four points five fewer than 15th-placed FC Koln, who are the first team outside of the relegation zone.

Head coach Alexander Blessin has only overseen six games as boss, winning twice and losing on three occasions, but his team have taken four points from the last nine on offer in the Bundesliga.

Their latest result was a 3-1 loss against Hamburger SV on November 6, though they did win two and drawn one of their prior three fixtures.

Die Fohlen may ranks as the division's worst defensive team having conceded 25 goals in nine games, but their return of 12 goals in the final third is the second best total in the bottom six.

While Gladbach were defeated in their first three home matches of 2026-27, they have since won once and settled for a stalemate once at Borussia Park, though they are still winless at the ground in the league this season (W0, D1, L3).

Dortmund could find themselves trailing Bayern by three points by the time they face Gladbach due to the fact the Bavarians play against FC Koln on Friday.

Niko Kovac will be delighted by his side's start to the campaign considering 21 points is their joint best tally after nine matchweeks in 13 seasons.

BVB's most recent result was a 2-1 success against Elversberg on November 7, and that was their fifth triumph in six contests.

The club scored at least two goals in five of those fixtures, and though they only managed to keep one clean sheet in that time, no club has conceded fewer goals in the Bundesliga (seven).

Black and Yellow were beaten 1-0 in the corresponding meeting in 2025-26, losing 1-0 at Borussia Park in May, but they emerged victorious in five of their previous six encounters with Gladbach.

Dortmund have taken eight points from a possible 12 on the road in the Bundesliga this term, while they have lost one, drawn two and won just one of their last four outings away from home in all competitions.

Borussia Monchengladbach form (all competitions):.

Borussia Dortmund Bundesliga form:.

Borussia Dortmund form (all competitions):.

Gladbach will have to contend with numerous absences, including suspended centre-back Ko Itakura and injured striker Tim Kleindienst.

Expect to see Kevin Diks, Philipp Sander and Fabio Chiarodia in the backline, while Isac Lidberg may be trusted to lead the line up front.

As for Dortmund, there are still doubts about the availability of centre-forward Serhou Guirassy, who could have to settle for a place on the bench in favour of Fabio Silva.

Jobe Bellingham and Felix Nmecha have often featured together, and they are the most likely duo to start together in a double pivot.

Emre Can is closing in on a return from a cruciate ligament injury, but he is not ready to play on Saturday, so perhaps fans will see a three-man defence consisting of Joane Gadou, Waldemar Anton and Nico Schlotterbeck.

Borussia Monchengladbach possible starting lineup:.

Nicolas; Diks, Sander, Chiarodia; Scally, Uno, Neuhaus, Castrop; Bolin, Lidberg, Mohya.

Borussia Dortmund possible starting lineup:.

Kobel; Gadou, Anton, Schlotterbeck; Beier, Bellingham, Nmecha, Svensson; Karetsas, Sabitzer; Silva.

It is difficult to look past Gladbach's poor defensive record given they are the most porous team in the division.

Even if Dortmund fail to keep a clean sheet, there is little evidence to suggest they will suffer a collapse at the back and drop points at Borussia Park.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Premier League and EFL are set to hold serious conversations about the blackout’s future next year with pretty much every TV slot now exhausted.

Removing the blackout – which is a rule that prevents live football matches from being broadcast on television or streaming services between 2.45pm and 5.15pm on Saturdays – could have a detrimental effect on attendances and finances, especially clubs in the lower tiers like Crawley Town.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

The blackout is under threat and television rights deals for the Premier League, EFL and Scottish Premiership are all up for renewal in 2029-30 and last year, Premier League chief executive Richard Masters said there were no plans to remove the blackout – introduced in 2003 by UEFA as Article 48.

According to recent reports, but this summer there appeared to be a shift in emphasis, with Masters saying there would be talks with the EFL ahead of the renewal of TV rights. Prime Minister Andy Burnham has urged caution and suggested the health of the football pyramid should come first.

In a recent development, the only leagues that apply Article 48 are England, Scotland and Northern Ireland. No other major country qualifies for the blackout - it is a tradition that is unique to football in the United Kingdom.

But how would it affect Crawley Town?

CEO Allman gave his personal opinion – and not necessarily that of the club – about the situation and what it would mean if it ended.

He mentioned: “My personal opinion is that the 3pm blackout currently works well in protecting the current football pyramid. I hear the arguments about it not being in place in other countries, but there is no pyramid like the UK pyramid so am not sure it is a fair comparison.

"We see notable increases in attendances during international breaks as well as drop offs for Tuesday night games for example where they are available on SkySports+ so in general, whilst removing the blackout, would arguably increase the exposure of clubs like Crawley, would levy that with actual attendances dropping off, which whilst having the obvious financial implication, will also have impacts on atmospheres and the general match-day feel.”.

It has been revealed that so it’s clear whether he would oppose the ending of the blackout? “I wouldn’t be in favour - as I say, I think the pyramid is what stands us apart from other countries and sports, and with that, would encourage fans to go out and experience the full pyramid, rather than looking for more Premier League games on TV.”.

He added: “Whilst I understand the argument of increased coverage, I wouldn’t levy that against supporters being in the stadium, buying a pint, eating a burger, cheering their team on and in turn, financially supporting the club to allow us to kick on across the board.”.

Lewes down Town to reach Sussex Senior Cup last eight

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • On a damp evening on the Sussex coast, Lewes defeated Step 4 Town 2-1 to make the last eight.
  • Two goals of varying difficulty from Bassett laid the foundations for the win, with the Rooks then withstanding Town’s pressure after a Sonny Walsh strike to make progress.
  • Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

On a damp evening on the Sussex coast, Lewes defeated Step 4 Town 2-1 to make the last eight.

Two goals of varying difficulty from Bassett laid the foundations for the win, with the Rooks then withstanding Town’s pressure after a Sonny Walsh strike to make progress.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

While it was not the most fluent outing for Lewes, several performances on an evening of experimentation will give reason for optimism.

The Rooks arrived at The Saffrons with six changes to their starting XI, including Josh Spinks’ return as captain and a debut for new attacking signing Kwesi Ntim.

Ntim, who has scored 20 goals in 33 games for Lingfield in 2026, was a bright spark early on, cutting in from the left flank and posing problems for the home defence.

Genuine chances took a while to arrive on the south coast, with the opening stages dominated by safe possession football.

After 25 minutes, however, Lewes created their first threat as Bassett worked space on the right and forced goalkeeper Chris Winterton to punch a cross into the path of Brian Garzon, whose right-footed effort was cleared off the line.

The Rooks slowly built the pressure from here, with Tyler Christian-Law and Mackenzie Richardson driving at goal before the opener soon arrived.

According to recent reports, in the 37th minute, Ntim added a flash of brilliance with a pacey drive in from the left, setting up Richardson for a first-time effort at goal. With ex-Rooks ‘keeper Winterton spilling the ball, Bassett was on hand to tap home.

Richardson had another bite at a goal of his own before the break, but Winterton stood up well to a rising effort from the left of the box to keep the score at 0-1.

Lewes did not hesitate in doubling down on their advantage at the start of the second half, and Bassett was the man to deliver again.

Barely 30 seconds into the half, the forward stormed down the right and cut into the box before producing an audacious chip on Winterton that dropped into the top left corner.

It was a moment of magic, and whether Bassett had meant it or not, nobody could begrudge the striker his fourth goal of the season thus far.

The Rooks got into a rhythm after this, regularly wriggling free of Town's attentions and finding space on the counter without truly putting the game to bed.

Bassett and Ntim were similarly denied in the area, while Garzon had at least two notable chances while cutting inside that flew inches wide of the post.

All the while, Town were never out of the tie, and they got their spark in the 61st minute.

Sonny Walsh was set free on the right of the box and blasted an effort past Louis Rogers to halve the deficit.

Town had two brilliant chances to level the scores in the final 30 minutes, but as has been their story in the last few weeks, luck was against them.

A ball in from the right was stabbed over the crossbar from close range, and in the dying stages, Walsh was again set free on the right but blasted over the target.

Equally, Lewes could have added to their advantage as substitute Omar Al-Seadi prodded wide of the left post when excellently teed up by a combination of Bassett and Kurtis Cumberbatch.

Altogether, Lewes were relieved to hear the final whistle as they made it to the final eight, but were good value for the result across the 90 minutes.

At the time of writing, the timing of the draw for the Quarter-Finals, and the dates of this round, are yet to be announced.

We anticipate news of both in due course, and urge supporters to keep tabs on our social media pages for the latest updates.

This Saturday, the Rooks are back in Isthmian Premier Division action away at Ramsgate FC.

With Lewes in 5th and Ramsgate - with a game in hand - just three points behind in 6th, it has all the makings of an excellent game at Southwood Stadium. Kick-off is at 3pm.

Lewes FC: Rogers; Mundele, Spinks (C), Hamstead, Cox (Allen, 69’); Christian-Law, Garzon, Richardson (Unwin, 76’); Fisher (Cumberbatch, 85’), Bassett (Mahmoud, 90’), Ntim (Al-Seadi, 69’).

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Carter White | 19 Nov 2026 13:37, Last updated: 19 Nov 2026 13:38.

Real Madrid have revealed that Aurelien Tchouameni has signed a contraction extension until June 2032.

The 26-year-old and Jose Mourinho's men have made a decent start to the 2026-27 campaign, with Los Blancos sitting second place in the La Liga standings, just three points behind arch rivals Barcelona.

Following the final international break of the calendar year, Real Madrid return to action at the Bernabeu on Saturday afternoon, when top-flight regulars Celta Vigo are the visitors in La Liga.

The makeup of Los Blancos' squad has shifted massively over the past few years as a number of new attacking stars have arrived, including French superstar Kylian Mbappe and England's Jude Bellingham.

With his influence waning, Vinicius Junior has endured a difficult start to the current campaign, with the Brazil international struggling since Real Madrid waved goodbye to German legend Toni Kroos.

Communicating to supporters worldwide on their official website, Real Madrid confirmed some exciting news involving Tchouameni, who has started seven La Liga matches so far in the 2026-27 term.

Los Blancos have announced that the 26-year-old has put pen to paper on a bumper contract extension at the Bernabeu, committing his long-term future to the 15-time European champions.

Tchouameni's deal with Real Madrid now expires in June 2032, meaning that the Frenchman could spend a decade at the Spanish giants if he sees out at the length of his recently-agreed terms.

The midfielder joined from Ligue 1 outfit Monaco in the summer of 2022 on a deal running until June 2028, meaning that he was approaching the conclusion of his initial agreement at the club.

Tchouameni started the La Liga victories over Barcelona (2-1), Racing Santander (3-0) and Valencia (3-0) prior to the November international break and should play once again versus Celta Vigo on Saturday.

Racking up over 200 competitive appearances since his 2022 arrival from France, Tchouameni has become part of the furniture at Real Madrid, who are looking to repeat their former glories.

The departure of legendary German Kroos left a massive hole to fill in the middle of the park, and Los Blancos are focused on bringing through the next generation of club heroes under head coach Mourinho.

Tchouameni featured in a staggering 55 matches across all competitions for Real Madrid last season, highlighting his importance to a side who have their work cut out chasing down Barcelona this term.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • By JOHN MCGARRY, SCOTTISH CHIEF SPORTS FEATURE WRITER.
  • Published: 17:06 EST, 16 November 2026 | Updated: 18:08 EST, 16 November 2026.
  • Despite re-establishing Scotland’s credentials as a credible football nation, by common consent, Steve Clarke’s time in charge of the side was up in the summer.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By JOHN MCGARRY, SCOTTISH CHIEF SPORTS FEATURE WRITER.

Published: 17:06 EST, 16 November 2026 | Updated: 18:08 EST, 16 November 2026.

Despite re-establishing Scotland’s credentials as a credible football nation, by common consent, Steve Clarke’s time in charge of the side was up in the summer.

With qualification for a major tournament no longer satisfying the desires of the Tartan Army, a seven-year itch led to a parting of the ways.

In order to take that elusive step into a knock-out round, the theory went that employing a bolder coach who’d get more out of the players was all that was required. So much for that.

According to recent reports, while few would dispute that a change at the helm was required, it was legitimate to question the wisdom in the SFA making one which was quite so radical. Those concerns have only been amplified by what’s been witnessed so far under Sebastien Pocognoli.

Recent findings suggest that the Belgian is young, smart and intense. He won a title in Belgium with Union Saint-Gilloise and will have taken much from his brief, ill-fated spell at Monaco. He wants to play the kind of football supporters long to see.

But this Nations League campaign has been nothing short of dismal. Two wins from six matches, both of those coming against a poor North Macedonia side, and three nights to forget against the Swiss and Slovenia, is a lamentable record.

Andy Robertson endured a miserable night on the occasion of his record-breaking 103rd cap.

Notwithstanding the fact that there were always likely to be teething problems, it’s fallen miles short of modest expectations.

Recent findings suggest that talk of it taking up to 18 months to all come up roses is all very well. But to believe that’s going to be the case, you need to see more green shoots at this point.

Having finished third in the section, Scotland are bound for pot three when the draw for Euro 2028 is made in Belfast next month.

Unless there’s a radical improvement come the qualifiers in March, it’s hard to see how Pocognoli’s side will get there by any means other than the back door.

This was another tough watch for the travelling supporters, one which will only lead to growing concerns about where all this is heading.

For half of a half, Scotland actually looked like they were getting somewhere under their upcoming manager.

Scotland boss Sebastien Pocognoli faces some serious questions over a miserable campaign.

In a recent development, from the minute Lewis Ferguson scored a horrible own goal, though, they became a rabble. Not nearly enough punch on the front foot. And far too easy to play through.

They shipped two goals inside five minutes early in the second half and looked like they’d have taken the final whistle there and then.

Individual mistakes from players are troubling Pocognoli in the same way they pockmarked the later days of Clarke’s reign.

Having witnessed Grant Hanley, Scott McKenna and Andy Robertson err in the World Cup, the Tartan Army had already seen Jack Hendry sent off against the Swiss at Hampden before Ferguson joined the growing list of sinners here.

Arriving midway through the first half, his unfathomable moment came when there wasn’t a red shirt in close proximity. It was a kick in the teeth for Pocognoli after a reasonable start.

While it would have been stretching matters to suggest that his team were vulnerable, Murat Yakin was without four of his massive hitters in Manuel Akanji, Johan Manzambi, Dan Ndoye and Granit Xhaka.

It has been revealed that there was a smattering of starters with five or six caps to their name. Two of the front three, Samuel Ballet and Winsley Boteli, were just 20.

Lewis Ferguson can't believe his misfortune after slicing the ball into his own net for the opener.

It was a night when Scottish football history was made with Robertson winning his 103rd cap to finally rise above his great friend, Sir Kenny Dalglish.

Pocognoli stuck by the back-three – Ryan Porteous, Luke Graham and Kieran Tierney – who acquitted themselves well against North Macedonia.

There was no great shock that the more defensive-minded Aaron Hickey replaced Ben Gannon-Doak on the right. Without a goal in 21 matches before a ball was kicked, Oli McBurnie’s selection ahead of Che Adams was intriguing.

The infuriating thing from Pocognoli’s perspective was that his side began with the right attitude.

Aside from an Isaac Schmidt shot which was fielded by Angus Gunn, they looked comfortable.

According to recent reports, john McGinn’s pass into McBurnie saw the Hull forward flick the ball into space for Hickey to chase. Just when it looked like he might get a shot away, he was caught.

The positive early approach was typified by Porteous flying into a tackle 30 yards from the Swiss goal and winning the ball.

Winsley Boteli enjoys the moment after putting the stylish Swiss two goals ahead on the night.

Had it not been for Hickey hesitating to pick out Scott McTominay’s run, the Napoli man would have been in on goal.

In a recent development, to put it mildly, the Swiss didn’t need an invitation to go down. The appropriately named Samuel Ballet was especially fond of the theatrics.

For a brief spell, Scotland had their opponents hemmed in. Pocognoli was miffed that two quick corners didn’t amount to anything.

Billy Gilmour probed and McTominay made key interceptions and sprayed passes. McGinn fired over.

Sources indicate that at the midway point in the first half, there was much to admire. Then disaster struck.

In a recent development, the Swiss did well to advance down the right. Zachary Athekame simply launched a cross into the box and hoped for the best.

Aaron Hickey endured a painful injury blow and could now face another spell on the sidelines.

With Ferguson running back towards goal and Porteous waiting to boot the ball to safety, there was no obvious danger.

Sources indicate that for reasons only he could explain, the Bologna man stretched out a leg and watched on in horror as the ball sailed past Gunn. All that hard work undone in one desperate moment.

According to recent reports, hickey passed up a chance to immediately level when he headed Robertson’s cross wide. It was to be the Brentford man’s last meaningful involvement before he felt his hamstring tighten. Nathan Patterson replaced him.

A gift of a goal gave the Swiss a boost. Boteli debuted himself at Alvyn Sanches’ cross. Gunn was untroubled.

Patterson did well to head Robertson’s deep cross back into the danger zone. McGinn’s header was straight into the arms of Yvon Mvogo.

For all Scotland were entitled to feel a little sore at being one down at the break, it could have been worse. The defence were completely static as Adrian Bajrami debuted himself at a header. It was a good thing, from Gunn’s point of view, that the defender missed the target.

Alvyn Sanches drills home Switzerland's third goal in what was an entirely one-sided contest.

Ferguson truly had a night to forget here. Within two minutes of the restart, he needlessly invited pressure when he introduced a ball straight out of play.

In a recent development, within seconds, with Porteous advanced, the Swiss broke down the left. Ballet fed Remo Freuler who returned the favour. Ballet rolled the ball towards goal from 12 yards with Boteli claiming the final touch. The visitors’ hopes of a VAR reprieve for offside were dashed.

And with that, the roof caved in. Patterson was dispossessed and Boteli worked the ball into the feet of Sanches. You could only admire the finish, but Scotland were an absolute mess in the build-up. It was threatening to get ugly.

With Tierney, Scotland’s best player on the night, lying on the deck, Ballet was only denied by Gunn. The Tartan Army looked at the clock and wished it was over.

With a minute remaining, a bad night got worse when Zeki Amdouni’s deflected shot beat Gunn.

It has been revealed that mercifully, this tortuous Nations League campaign can now be consigned to history. It’s been the most chastening experience for all concerned.

By Carter White | 19 Nov 2026 14:04.

Manchester United head coach Mauricio Pochettino has reportedly prepared to enter talks over the Old Trafford future of Bruno Fernandes.

The 54-year-old Argentine arrives at the Theatre of Dreams with the Red Devils sitting 18th in the Premier League table after winning just one of their opening 10 top-flight games of 2026-27.

That woeful run was eventually enough to remove Michael Carrick from his post at Man Utd, with the club's hierarchy moving quickly to lure Pochettino away from his duties with the United States on the international scene.

As well as Carrick, wonderkid JJ Gabriel has also departed the Red Devils this month, with the teenage sensation set to sign for European giants Real Madrid despite failing to make a first-team appearance for United.

Looking to avoid an unthinkable relegation this season, Man Utd are plotting significant additions to the playing squad during the January transfer window, with a Greek striker supposedly catching the eye.

According to transfer specialist Fabrizio Romano via Football Transfers, new Manchester United head coach Pochettino is set to be immediately involved in major talks at the Theatre of Dreams.

The report states that the Red Devils and captain Fernandes have been locked in discussions over a contract extension for the past five months, with an agreement yet to be reached by the two parties.

The 32-year-old's current deal at Old Trafford expires in June 2027, meaning that the Portuguese playmaker would be able to depart on a free transfer at the conclusion of this season.

It is understood that Man Utd are aiming to avoid that scenario, and now incoming boss Pochettino is set to join talks with the player and the club over the future of the influential attacker.

Fernandes supposedly retains interest from clubs in Italy, Saudi Arabia and Turkey, with Champions League-competing Galatasaray attempting to bring the former Sporting Lisbon man to Istanbul over the summer.

Whilst Manchester United's transfer activity since the exit of Sir Alex Ferguson has come under deserved criticism, there is no doubt that the signing of Fernandes was an excellent move by the fallen English powerhouses.

The 32-year-old has been an almost ever-present in the Red Devils ranks since joining from the Primeira Liga in January 2020, scoring 113 goals across a total of 341 competitive appearances.

Fernandes broke the Premier League assist record last season despite his side's immense struggles, and that theme of shining amid the chaos extends throughout the attacker's time in England.
